RagShortTexts: The standing military of Angles in 374 AD relied upon veteran formations specialized in disciplined field deployment.
Combining heavy protective armor with specialized assault weaponry, the troops executed tactical doctrines honed in frontier engagements.
Commanders emphasized coordinated shock charges and defensive stability, preventing frontline collapse against aggressive cavalry raids.

Variants.Content: The martial renown of Angles rested upon exhaustive drilling and veteran battlefield cohesion during the turbulent close of the 4th century. Core tactical doctrine integrated heavy shield formations with disciplined skirmishing wings, executing tactical maneuvers designed to absorb and counter enemy shock. Along vulnerable sectors, defensive engineers implemented field fortifications and obstacles, breaking the initial momentum of hostile assaults. Once enemy ranks faltered, armored shock reserves counter-charged under thunderous horn blasts, crushing exposed flanks with heavy swords and barbed spears. This balance of resilient endurance and ferocious striking power formed the military bedrock preserving Angles against overwhelming regional adversaries.

Spearmen on the shore wall brace behind their shields as the horns sound, and the front rank lowers its spears to meet the enemy's charge. The men in the second rank push forward to fill the gaps, while the archers wait for the sergeant's signal. Anyone who breaks from the line will be struck down by his own comrades before he reaches the rear.

The Anglian war council has settled the battle order for the coastal campaign, placing the heavy infantry at the center and the mounted riders on the flanks. Supply must reach the fort before the spring tides flood the causeway. Send the order by a sworn courier, and keep a second copy in a sealed chest, because a single lost dispatch can ruin the whole attack.
